newsitem.title: POLAND: BRE, Germany's ADIG to start fund firm.
newsitem.headline: BRE, Germany's ADIG to start fund firm.

text.p: Poland's Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA (BRE) and Germany's Allgemeine Deutsche Investment GmbH (ADIG) agreed to set up a joint fund management firm, expected to start operation by mid-1997, BRE's deputy head said.

"Today we signed an agreement with ADIG on a joint venture, under which we plan to establish a trust fund company, which will start operation in the first half of 1997," Wojciech Kostrzewa told a news conference.
ADIG is jointly owned by Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Commerzbank AG, both holding 40 percent stakes.

Commerzbank has a 21 percent stake in BRE. Kostrzewa said BRE and ADIG, one of the largest German fund management firms, planned to invest together 18 million German marks in the company in which BRE would have 60 percent and ADIG 40 percent.

He said the new fund company, which would still have to win an operating licence from the Polish Securities Commission, would strive to offer a broad range of open-ended funds to the public with varying levels of risk.
He said, however, it was not yet decided whether the company would start operating with just one fund or a family of products.
Friedrich Pfeiffer, ADIG's board member, also present, said the joint venture would combine BRE's knowledge of the Polish market and ADIG's long experience in managing funds.
"We want to bring together in the new company BRE's know-how in respect to the Polish business and ADIG's know how of banking and financial management," Pfeiffer said.
Kostrzewa said the new company, whose name he declined to reveal, would strive to capture at least a 14-percent market share.
"Our mid-term, five-year plan is to reach the same market share as ADIG has in German, which is 14 percent," he said.
Kostrzewa said that over a longer term the new company would consider investing in neighbouring countries and other OECD countries.
